state.case_summary:
A woman in her 30s presented to the emergency department after a generalized tonic-clonic seizure lasting 3 minutes. She had no seizure disorder but had a left cerebral ischemic stroke and myocardial infarction 4 months ago with use of synthetic cannabis with resolution of symptoms and neurologic deficits. The patient's friend reported she used synthetic cannabis just before the seizure.

Glasgow Coma Scale score of 9, moved all extremities, appeared to be in pain, was afebrile, and had stable vital signs. The patient developed another tonic-clonic seizure, which aborted with medication.

- Laboratory tests: Glucose level 133 mg/dL. Normal complete blood cell count, chemistry panel, aspirin level, acetaminophen level, alcohol level, and liver function tests. Urine drug screen positive for cannabinoids.- Imaging studies:   Image Title: Axial and Coronal Magnetic Resonance Images of the Brain  Image Description: The images reveal diffuse bilateral cortical and subcortical edema in cortical and subcortical white matter bilaterally.

What is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. Post-Stroke Seizure Disorder (Epilepsy)
B. Reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (RCVS)
C. Synthetic Cannabinoid–Induced Toxic Encephalopathy
D. Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES)
